finalText:
Found it: `src/jobs/processOrder.js` acquired a connection but only released it on success — a rejected order left the connection held forever.

`processOrder` bypassed the shared `withConnection` wrapper and called `pool.release` after `await run(...)`, so any thrown error skipped that line. The worker logs show exactly this: failed orders piling up pool usage until it hit 5/5 and the worker gave up.

Fixed by wrapping the acquire in `try/finally`, same pattern the API handler already used safely. All 4 tests pass now, 84ms.
